questions.title: What exactly is NormalFloat (NF4) quantization and why is it considered information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights?
questions.question_body: I read that NF4 was introduced specifically for zero-centered normal distributions coming from pretrained LLM weights, but I don't understand how its equal-probability bin design differs from ordinary integer based k-bit quantisation or floating-point scaling—that seems crucial.

questions.title: Why does NF₄ outperform regular FP₄ during finetuning despite both being only four bits wide?
questions.question_body: The experiments repeatedly report higher perplexity scores when using NF₄ instead of float-based k-bit representations—there should be an intuitive explanation for the empirical advantage arising purely from statistical bin placement.
